blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-2 (A dropped webhook is only logged at debug level, in free text) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, capped), or better, hand failed deliveries to a delayed retry queue. As written, when a merchant's server returns 5xx or is briefly unreachable, the five POSTs are sent immediately one after another: a restart of a few seconds exhausts every attempt and the event is lost, while a merchant under load receives a burst of retries for every payment event (a retry storm across all its events). Also stop retrying on non-retryable 4xx responses (other than 408/429), which the loop currently retries identically.
findings.title: Retries fire back-to-back with no backoff

findings.recommendation: Use the project's structured `logger` (src/logger.ts, as src/events.ts does) instead of `console.debug`: log each failed attempt with fields (eventId, merchant/payment id, URL host, attempt, HTTP status or error) and log the final drop at error level, plus a counter metric for delivered/failed/dropped webhooks. Today, when a merchant endpoint is down, debug output is typically filtered in production, so the event is permanently lost and nobody — operator or merchant — knows. A non-ok HTTP response (`response.ok` false) is not logged at all, so the status code that would explain the failure is never visible.
findings.title: A dropped webhook is only logged at debug level, in free text

findings.recommendation: `publish` in src/events.ts awaits each listener in turn, so a merchant endpoint that times out holds the dispatch of that event — and every listener after this one — for up to 5 × 5 s = 25 s (more once backoff is added). Whether this stalls the payment service depends on whether its caller awaits `publish`, which the change does not show. Consider dispatching delivery asynchronously (a queue or a fire-and-forget task with its own error handling).
findings.title: Delivery retries block the payment event dispatch loop
